In this section, we point out some other long-distance trails in the part of the Apennines lying between the Taro and the Scrivia.

Some itineraries have been opened ex novo, while others follow ancient paths, like ours. Sometimes they are non-profit undertakings, while at other times there is a commercial purpose, direct or indirect.

But it does not matter: all these routes have something unique to offer and represent a sort of natural (and spiritual) complement for anyone who has fallen in love with the Antica via del Cifalco.

  • La Via del Sale/Via del Mare: a spectacular trail that follows the ridge of M. Antola (indeed it retraces the old “Via dell’Antola”) and which, in four days, leads from Varzi (Pavia, Lombardy) to Portofino Mare. The last stretch, from the Passo dei Casetti onwards, coincides with the itinerary of the Via del Cifalco as proposed here (not counting our exits and variants).
  • Alta via dei Monti Liguri (AVML): a great classic for crossing Liguria from west to east (or vice versa), from the Maritime Alps to Ceparana, in Lunigiana. No fewer than 43 stages for a very long and demanding route, but one hard to match for immersiveness. The Via del Cifalco overlaps with it for a short stretch, between Barbagelata and the Passo della Scoglina.
  • Sentiero dei Celti e dei Liguri: a recently conceived trail from Milan to the sea, running along the crest of the upper Val Nure and descending to Sestri Levante. 10 stages for a total of 222 kilometres.
  • Via degli Abati (VA): a historic itinerary linking Pavia to Pontremoli, passing through some of the main historic villages of the Apennines, such as Bobbio. It cuts across the Apennines from west to east, for about 194 kilometres, with a total ascent of about 8,000 metres.
  • Anello dei Borghi (Alta Val Nure): a stunning loop conceived by our friend Giacomo Bracchi, through the little-visited villages of the Alta Val Nure. It lies entirely within the municipality of Ferriere (Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna), along 11 kilometres of nature, ancient stone villages, streams and chestnut woods.
  • Via Marialonga: we move decidedly into the Parma area for this long trail that leads from Fornovo Taro to Sestri Levante in seven stages. Congratulations to our friend Carlo Serventi for this project, born and run with passion and sincerity.
  • Itinerario Storico Colombiano: after a long period of neglect, the path linking Terrarossa Colombo (Moconesi, Liguria) to Quinto genovese has been restored, passing through the “fasce” (terraces) behind Genova Nervi. It is about 19 kilometres, following what was historically the route of the family of Christopher Columbus’s ancestors along the very ancient mule track that ran from the Val Fontanabuona to Genoa.
  • Itinerario dei Feudi Fliscani (IFF): a recently conceived itinerary, but one that explores some of the areas historically under the rule of the Fieschi family for many centuries, in medieval times. From the Chiesa di San Giacomo at Gattorna, it climbs up to Monte Lavagnola (about five hours, 928 metres of ascent) through the wild Valle del Neirone. Today it is not in very good condition: it will also be up to those who read us to commit themselves to the restoration of this route of great historical, natural and hiking potential.
